author: TeIq
content:
## Source
.design/m5/44-mobile-app.md — REQ-3, AC-3 + decomposition PR 5.

## Surface
- Two new endpoints on `polaris-backend/src/api/cases.rs`:
  - `POST /api/cases/{incident_id}/take-ownership` → bumps v1 case lock to current moderator
  - `POST /api/cases/{incident_id}/release-ownership` → releases v1 case lock
- WebSocket broadcasts the ownership change via the existing v1 case-lock channel (already wired in v1 issue #57 / WebSocket live-feed).
- Mobile UI: two buttons on the read-only case view ("Take" / "Release"). Disabled when offline (REQ-7 / AC-7).

## Rust-quality notes
- **Reuse v1 case-lock plumbing.** Per architect skill: don't fork the lock mechanism for mobile. The mobile endpoints call the same `case_locks::claim()` and `case_locks::release()` functions desktop already uses (rust-quality §9 — single source of truth).
- **Idempotent.** Taking ownership of an already-owned incident (by the same moderator) is a no-op success. Taking ownership of an incident locked by ANOTHER moderator returns `409 Conflict`. Tested.
- **WebSocket broadcast on success** — the existing case-lock change event fans out to all connected clients. Desktop reflects in <2s per AC-3.
- **Per rust-quality §3**: handlers return `Result<axum::Json<TakeOwnershipResponse>, ApiError>` with proper error mapping. The `409 Conflict` case maps from `LockError::AlreadyHeld { holder: ModeratorId }`.
- **No `MutexGuard` across `.await`** in the case-lock code (per rust-quality §10). Already a v1 constraint; this PR doesn't relax it.

## External references
- v1 case-lock impl: `polaris-backend/src/repo/case_locks.rs` (existing)
- v1 WebSocket broadcast: `polaris-backend/src/api/websocket.rs` (existing, issue #57)
- axum response patterns: https://docs.rs/axum/0.8/axum/response/index.html

## Acceptance (AC-3)
- [ ] Mobile moderator A takes ownership of incident 42. Desktop moderator B's case-list view shows "owned by A" within 2s.
- [ ] Mobile moderator A taps Release. Desktop view updates to "unowned" within 2s.
- [ ] Concurrent take by A and B: B receives `409`, A holds the lock.

- Blocks #120 (call-senior reads the on-call schedule + needs ownership context).
